To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

CPT violation via the ``Ether'' potential can solve the solar neutrinos and LSND anomaly, while respecting the constraints imposed by the current neutrino experiments, only if m \not= \bar{m} is also assumed.

(i) CPT violating ``ether'' potentials can not solve all electron anti-neutrinos puzzles, (ii) they can be severely constrained by the current neutrino oscillation data, (iii) they can be even better constrained by future neutrino oscillations experiments, and that (iv) they are still a viable alternative to the sterile neutrinos paradigm when it comes to explaining the LSND anomaly, if one is willing to give up the explanation of the solar neutrino problem.

the LSND anomaly cannot be solved in the context of a two-flavor neutrino model with CPT violating ether potentials, and that the current neutrino oscillation data already provide some of the tightest bounds on CPT violating terms in the neutrino oscillation probability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to the neutrino oscillation puzzle, which may provide an alternative to the sterile neutrino hypothesis.
the possibility to solve the solar and LSND puzzles by means of Lorentz-violation, which would be a rather interesting alternative to the standard sterile neutrino solution.
the question of how much information about the neutrino sector can be extracted from the current and future neutrino data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, while it is not yet possible to exclude CPT violation in the neutrino oscillation sector, the prospects are not particularly encouraging either.
CPT violation in neutrinos is disfavored by neutrino oscillation data.
, while the possibility of a CPT violating neutrino sector is not excluded by the neutrino data, it is not favored by them either.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, if CPT violation in the neutrino oscillation sector is due to the presence of an ether, then the ether is constrained to be much more symmetric and isotropic than the standard model Higgs field.
the neutrino sector can be used as an important probe for testing Lorentz invariance.

CPT violation via Ether potentials cannot solve the LSND anomaly, and is severely constrained by the current data, but could still be a viable option if the neutrino sector is extended to include sterile neutrinos.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current data already rule out the simplest Lorentz-invariant CPT violating models.
CPT violation via the Ether potential cannot be the sole explanation for the LSND anomaly and solar neutrino deficit.

, while it is not possible to reconcile the solar neutrino data with the LSND anomaly by introducing CPT violating terms in a two-flavor like analysis, it might still be possible to reconcile these data by introducing CPT violation in the three-flavor case.
